Database software and related tables

Unit 2 · Week 1 · Lesson 3 · Suggested 55-minute plan; adjust to local timing.

Prepare: Open the database foundations chapter, equipment-loans-flat.csv, database-foundations-workbook.md and database-foundations-answers.md. Use paper or a school-approved spreadsheet. No SQL installation or student account is needed. Use the fixed reporting date of 8 April 2026. Teacher notes and explained answers are public.

Suggested answers are teacher guidance, not extra assessment tasks. These notes are public.

1. Database software and related tables

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Learning intention

Introduce the equipment desk scenario. Distinguish stored records from the software that manages them. Activities are ungraded. Use only the supplied fictional loan records. Suggested timings are flexible. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-foundations.

2. A home for a fact

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Individual recall, then partner explanation

Equipment stores the item description. Loan stores an event’s due date. Ask learners to explain why an item can have different due dates in different borrowing events. Recall the separate responsibilities from Lesson 2. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-foundations.

3. Three terms, different roles

Suggested time: 6 minutes

Instructional strategy: Worked table and discussion

DBMS means database management system. RDBMS means relational database management system. The equipment desk’s records are the database. A DBMS is the software that defines, retrieves and changes managed data. An RDBMS is a type of DBMS that uses relations, commonly introduced as tables. PostgreSQL is an example. Source: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/tutorial-concepts.html . Every RDBMS is a DBMS, but DBMS is the broader term. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-foundations.

4. A request to the software

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Teacher model with student predictions

Describe the flow in words and ask students to label user/application, DBMS and stored database in a simple paper sketch. A system may check access and data constraints before an update. Facilities depend on the product and configuration. Do not imply that every DBMS automatically enforces the desk’s intended permissions. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-foundations.

5. The three-table sketch

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Paired practice with exchanged roles

Use workbook questions 7–9. Borrower holds the label, Equipment the description, Loan the due date and references. LoanID identifies an event because a borrower can borrow the same item again. Sketch labels and links only. Formal keys and relationship notation follow in later chapters. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-foundations.

6. One file, several related tables

Suggested time: 12 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent application

SQLite is an embedded SQL database engine and a single file can contain multiple tables. Source: https://www.sqlite.org/about.html . Flat-file organisation concerns the logical structure of records, not simply the number of physical files. Students should distinguish the SQLite software from the file of stored records. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-foundations.

7. A file-count misconception

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Choice and explanation

B. The existence of related tables is compatible with one physical database file. A CSV loan register and a SQLite database file need not have the same logical organisation. Ask learners to explain the distinction rather than choosing by file extension alone. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-foundations.

8. A sentence for each term

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Reflection and a fresh example

Example: the organised equipment and loan records form the database. The DBMS software manages requests to those records. An RDBMS is a DBMS using the relational model. Accept equivalent explanations that keep data and software distinct. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-foundations.
